# Understanding Cairns: A Summary

## Core Concept
A cairn is a structure that grows through pulses. The growth isn't linear—taller cairns grow more because the pulse mechanism depends on current height.

## Rule C1: The Pulse
When you pulse a cairn, it grows by the stride amount plus a bonus. The bonus is how many complete strides fit into the current height (before pulsing). So a 20-mark cairn with stride 6 gains 6 + 3 = 9 marks (since 20 ÷ 6 gives 3 complete strides).

## Rule C2: Repeated Pulses
You can't just multiply one pulse's growth. Each pulse must be calculated fresh from the new height, because the stride-count changes. A cairn that gains 9 marks in pulse 1 might gain 10 in pulse 2 if it got taller.

## Rule C3: The Leak
A leak damages the cairn *after* the pulse completes. You divide the pulsed height by the leak size and lose that many marks. The leak is applied to the new height, not the original.

## Rule C4: Finding Origins
You can work backwards uniquely from a final height through multiple pulses. For each pulse you undo, you find what height would produce the result you see. There's exactly one answer because pulses are monotonic—they always make things grow.

## Rule C5: The Drain
A drain is a fixed amount lost each cycle. Unlike a leak (which depends on height), drain removes the same number every time. The cairn continues cycling through pulses and drains until it empties. Simple division doesn't work because pulse amounts vary.

## Rule C6: Merging
Two cairns can combine into one using weighted shares and a tether. Each cairn contributes a fraction (expressed as tenths) to the merged height. The tether adds or subtracts based on the shorter cairn's height. Merging isn't just averaging—the tether makes the relationship complex.
